item.title: Gasoline in Switzerland: reserves open, effects on prices
item.description: Mandatory open stocks for petrol and diesel. From 8 to 20 September 2026 withdrawal up to 30,000 m³. Low-level Cressier and Reno refinery shutdown.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Mandatory open stocks for petrol and diesel - From 8 to 20 September 2026 withdrawal up to 30,000 m³ - Low-level Cressier and Reno refinery shutdown - Less than 3% of total reserves, no alarm
## Key facts - **What**: Temporary withdrawal from mandatory gasoline and diesel stocks - When: from 8 to 20 September 2026 - Where: Switzerland, with effects on the Ticino market - Who: Federal Office for Economic Supply - Amount: up to 30,000 m³ of petrol and the same amount of diesel - Percentage: less than 3% of required reserves - Reason: Cressier refinery shutdown and difficulty on the Rhine
The Confederation has opened strategic fuel reserves. On September 8, 2026, the Federal Office for Economic Supply authorized the temporary withdrawal from mandatory gasoline and diesel stocks to support the market and ensure continuity of supply. The decision comes after the shutdown of the Cressier refinery, in the Canton of Neuchâtel, and the difficulties of transport on the Rhine.
For those who cross the border every day to work in Ticino, the news deserves attention. The withdrawal period runs from 8 to 20 September, with a maximum amount of 30,000 cubic metres of petrol and the same amount of diesel. According to the Confederation, this figure represents less than 3% of their respective mandatory stocks. No alert on availability, but the situation must be monitored.
### Because the ### Cosa cambia per chi attraversa il confine
Il frontaliere che ogni mattina parte dall'Italia verso il Ticino con il permesso G in tasca ha una variabile in più da considerare: il prezzo della benzina. La decisione della Confederazione non modifica le aliquote fiscali né tocca l'imposta alla fonte, ma incide su una voce di spesa quotidiana.
Consideriamo il quadro. La raffineria di Cressier copre poco più del 30% del fabbisogno nazionale. Il Reno, che è la via principale per i prodotti petroliferi, ha livelli d'acqua bassi. Le riserve strategiche ora sono parzialmente aperte. Cosa significa in pratica? Che per due settimane il mercato avrà una valvola di sfogo, ma i prezzi potrebbero comunque salire se la raffineria non riprende presto.
Per chi percorre 40-60 chilometri al giorno tra andata e ritorno, un aumento di 5-10 centesimi al litro può significare 15-25 franchi in più al mese. Non è una cifra enorme, ma si somma ad altre voci: l'AVS, la LPP, la LAMal. Il budget del frontaliere è fatto di tanti piccoli tasselli.
### Confronto con la situazione precedente
Prima del fermo di Cressier, il mercato era già sotto pressione per il Reno. Ora, con le riserve aperte, la disponibilità è garantita ma non illimitata. I 30.000 metri cubi di benzina e altrettanti di gasolio rappresentano meno del 3% delle scorte obbligatorie. Una goccia nel mare, ma sufficiente a evitare il panico.
Il periodo critico va dall'8 al 20 settembre. Dopo quella data, se la raffineria non avrà risolto il problema tecnico, la situazione potrebbe tornare tesa. I frontalieri che hanno la possibilità di fare rifornimento in Italia, dove i prezzi sono spesso più bassi, potrebbero valutare questa opzione. Ma attenzione: la convenienza dipende dal tasso di cambio CHF/EUR e dal tempo perso in coda ai valichi come Brogeda o Gaggiolo.
### Scenari possibili
Scenario uno: la raffineria riprende entro fine settembre, il Reno si rialza, i prezzi restano stabili. Scenario due: il fermo si prolunga, le riserve si esauriscono, i prezzi salgono. In entrambi i casi, il frontaliere deve essere pronto. Monitorare i prezzi, pianificare gli spostamenti, considerare il car pooling con colleghi che vivono nella stessa zona.
La decisione della Confederazione è un segnale di attenzione verso il mercato, ma non elimina l'incertezza. Per chi lavora in Canton Ticino, la benzina è un costo fisso. Conoscere la situazione attuale aiuta a prendere decisioni informate. E se i prezzi salgono, conviene verificare se il proprio datore di lavoro offre contributi per le spese di trasporto o se esistono agevolazioni per i pendolari.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Cosa fare nelle prossime due settimane
Il periodo critico va dall'8 al 20 settembre. Ecco una procedura pratica per il frontaliere che vuole gestire la situazione senza farsi cogliere impreparato.
**Passo 1: monitorare i prezzi.** Controlla ogni due giorni i listini delle stazioni di servizio in Ticino, in particolare quelle lungo la A2 e nei pressi dei valichi di Chiasso e Brogeda. Se vedi aumenti superiori a 5 centesimi al litro, valuta se fare rifornimento in Italia prima di entrare in Svizzera.
Passo 2: pianificare il pieno. Se hai un'auto con serbatoio da 50 litri, un pieno in Italia ti fa risparmiare circa 5-8 franchi rispetto alla Svizzera, a seconda del cambio. Ma considera il tempo in coda al confine: se aspetti 20 minuti a Brogeda, il risparmio si riduce. Meglio fare il pieno nelle ore meno trafficate, ad esempio la sera o il sabato mattina.
Passo 3: valutare alternative. Se la situazione peggiora, il car pooling con altri frontalieri della tua zona può ridurre i costi del 30-50%. Anche i mezzi pubblici sono un'opzione: il trasporto transfrontaliero da Como a Mendrisio o Lugano funziona, ma richiede più tempo. Per molti, l'auto resta la scelta più pratica.
Passo 4: controllare il budget. Un aumento di 10 centesimi al litro sulla benzina incide sul tuo stipendio netto. Usa il [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator) per verificare come le spese extra influiscono sul tuo reddito disponibile. Se hai un margine ridotto, potresti dover rivedere altre voci di spesa.
### Strumenti utili
Per chi vuole capire meglio la propria situazione finanziaria da frontaliere, il [simulatore di busta paga](nav:payslip) è uno strumento efficace. Ti aiuta a vedere quanto incide ogni spesa variabile, inclusa la benzina, sul tuo netto mensile. Se invece vuoi confrontare i costi complessivi tra vivere in Italia e lavorare in Svizzera, il [confronto costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living) ti dà una fotografia chiara.
### Scadenze da ricordare
La finestra di prelievo delle riserve chiude il 20 settembre. Dopo quella data, la Confederazione valuterà se estendere il provvedimento o se la situazione è rientrata. Nel frattempo, tieni d'occhio le comunicazioni ufficiali dell'Ufficio federale per l'approvvigionamento economico e i siti di informazione locale.
Non c'è motivo di fare scorte: la Confederazione ha garantito la disponibilità. Ma la prudenza non guasta. Se i prezzi iniziano a salire, agisci con calma: un pieno in più in Italia non risolve la situazione, ma può farti risparmiare qualche franco. E ogni franco risparmiato è un franco in più nel tuo budget mensile di frontaliere.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/newsblog/valute-e-frontiere/1949618/benzina-la-svizzera-apre-le-riserve-cosa-puo-succedere-ai-prezzi-per-i-frontalieri)*

item.title: Culture in Switzerland, record number of companies but jobs fall
item.description: In 2024, cultural enterprises in Switzerland reach 69,441, setting a record, but jobs and company size fall.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Record number of cultural enterprises in Switzerland in 2024 - Growth higher than that of the total economy - Decline in employment in the cultural sector - Decrease in average company size
## Key facts - **What**: Trend in cultural enterprises and employment - When: Year 2024 - Where: Switzerland - Who: Federal Statistical Office (FSO) - Amount: 69,441 cultural enterprises in 2024
The Swiss economic and business landscape has reached a historic milestone in the cultural sector, although accompanied by employment dynamics that differ from the past. Never before in the Confederation has such a high number of enterprises operating in this field been recorded. During 2024, companies active in the cultural sector reached 69,441, setting a record figure that highlights particularly dynamic progression. This expansion proves to be superior to the growth recorded by the Swiss economy as a whole, outlining a continuously evolving and increasingly fragmented productive fabric.
### FSO statistical data
Official details released by the Federal Statistical Office (FSO) allow for an analysis of the medium-term trend. Since 2011, the total number of cultural enterprises has marked an increase of 27%. Over the same period, the entire Swiss economy instead recorded a more modest increase, stopping at 16%. Consequently, the market share represented by cultural enterprises out of the total number of companies operating nationwide went from 9.8% recorded in the initial reference period up to 10.7% in 2024. This increase in business density reflects a profound structural transformation, which also involves professionals active in the cross-border region and local labor market dynamics. Despite the strong expansion in the number of companies, the Swiss cultural sector is facing a less favorable situation in terms of employment. During 2024, the total number of available jobs in the sector fell to 241,025, showing a 0.9% decrease compared to the previous year's data. This represents a significant trend reversal, as it is the first decline in employment levels recorded since 2020. This dynamic is explained by the very nature of recent business growth, characterized by the birth of new entities that are smaller on average than in the past.
### Business size and economic weight
Analyzing the organizational structure, it clearly emerges that cultural enterprises have progressively become smaller. In 2011, each individual company employed an average of 4.1 workers, while in 2024 this average value dropped to 3.5. A similar decline is also observed when calculating full-time equivalents per enterprise, which decreased from 2.9 to 2.3 units. This dimensional contraction is not reflected in the rest of the Swiss economy, where a similar reduction in the average size of companies has not been witnessed. Consequently, over the long term, the overall weight of culture on the country's total employment has also decreased: the sector indeed accounted for 4.7% of all jobs in 2011, a percentage that dropped to 4.2% in 2024.
### The transformation of sectors and digital media
Growth has not been uniform across the various branches of the cultural industry. Between 2023 and 2024, the largest numerical increases in companies were concentrated in the audiovisual, multimedia, and advertising sectors, as well as in activities related to cultural heritage and the performing arts. The situation in traditional markets was the opposite: the book and press sector recorded a contraction of over 3% in 2024 compared to the previous year, highlighting a deficit of 12.3% fewer businesses when compared to the pre-pandemic period of 2019. To learn more about how these changes affect the labor market and professional opportunities in the border area, you can consult the dedicated [job listings](nav:jobs) section.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). The ongoing transition towards digitalization and multimedia is profoundly modifying the skills required in the Swiss cultural and economic sector. For professionals and workers operating or intending to operate between neighboring Italy and Switzerland, monitoring the evolution of these emerging sectors is essential to guide their professional choices. The progressive digitalization of advertising and audiovisual activities requires highly specialized profiles, while the contraction of traditional print media imposes a reflection on long-term employment prospects in historical publishing sectors.
### Tax and salary verifications
Labor market evolution and the creation of new micro-enterprises in the cultural sector entail the need to correctly manage one's contribution and tax position. Those who work or intend to start an independent or subordinate activity in Switzerland must pay particular attention to withholding taxes, mandatory social security contributions, and wage differences between various cantons. Accurately assessing one's net salary and the impact of current regulations allows for better planning of cross-border professional activities without surprises.
### Useful tools and calculators
To analyze income in detail, correctly estimate the tax burden, and understand the impact of taxes on earnings derived from collaborations or employment in Switzerland, available simulation tools can be used. For a precise and updated estimate of wages and tax burdens, check your economic situation now using the [salary calculator](nav:calculator).

item.title: Alto Piemonte: 6,470 hires expected in September 2026
item.description: The labour market in Upper Piedmont has 6,470 contracts scheduled for September 2026, with more than 75% of forward contracts.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 6,470 planned hires in Alto Piemonte for September 2026 - Over 75% of scheduled contracts will be temporary - Between 38% and 46% of companies report recruitment difficulties
## Key facts - **What**: Hiring forecasts for the month of September - When: September 2026 compared to September 2025 - Where: Biella, Novara, Verbano Cusio Ossola and Vercelli - Who: Unioncamere, Ministry of Labour and Monte Rosa Laghi Alto Piemonte Chamber of Commerce - Amount: 6,470 total scheduled contracts
The Alto Piemonte labor market is preparing to face the month of September 2026 with a total volume of 6,470 contracts planned by local businesses distributed across the provinces of Biella, Novara, Verbano Cusio Ossola and Vercelli. The data, processed by the Studies Service of the Monte Rosa Laghi Alto Piemonte Chamber of Commerce based on the monthly bulletin of the Excelsior Information System of Unioncamere and the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, marks a minimal variation compared to the same period of the previous year, recording just 10 fewer contracts across the entire reference territory. The intercepted figure represents exactly 18.2 percent of the total hires forecast in the entire Piedmont region.
### Territorial analysis of Excelsior data
Within the individual provinces, the distribution of employment flows shows different dynamics and volumes. In Novara, the picture is growing with 3,340 expected hires, recording 100 more positions than in September 2025 and confirming itself as the main economic engine of the area. In Vercelli, expected hires stand at 1,230, maintaining the exact same volume recorded twelve months earlier. In Biella, forecasts indicate 1,120 hires, highlighting a decrease of 40 units compared to the previous September. Finally, in Verbano Cusio Ossola, planned hires are 780, marking a drop of 70 jobs compared to the data recorded in 2025. Overall, labor demand therefore remains solid but diversified, with leading sectors such as accommodation and food services, commerce and personal services continuing to express a consistent share of the overall employment requirement, while reflecting the economic and territorial specificities of each individual province examined by the Excelsior survey. A more in-depth analysis of the contractual structure highlights how the predominant typology in Upper Piedmont remains firmly tied to precariousness or, in any case, temporary flexibility. In all four provinces considered, in fact, fixed-term contracts exceed the threshold of seventy-five percent of the total hires planned for the month of September. In more detail, the province of Novara provides a share of stable contracts equal to twenty-two percent, leaving seventy-eight percent to temporary work forms. In Biella, the ratio sees twenty-five percent of stable contracts against seventy-five percent of fixed-term contracts. Even more unbalanced values are recorded in Verbano Cusio Ossola and Vercelli, where just nineteen percent of open positions offer immediate stabilization, while eighty-one percent of contracts are configured as fixed-term. This strong prevalence of temporary relationships directly affects the employment prospects of those looking for stable employment in the area.
### Critical issues in hiring and the need for experience
A second significant element emerging from chamber data concerns the persistent difficulty of companies in finding personnel with adequate requirements on the market. The percentage of companies reporting problems in finding the requested profiles varies considerably depending on the province: it goes from thirty-eight percent recorded in Vercelli up to the peak of forty-six percent detected in Verbano Cusio Ossola, while Biella stands at forty-four percent and Novara at forty percent. This difficulty clashes with a very precise request from the productive fabric: companies predominantly look for workers who already possess specific professional experience or experience gained in the same employment sector. This specific need affects sixty-three point eight percent of profiles in Verbano Cusio Ossola, sixty point one percent in Vercelli, fifty-eight point eight percent in Biella, and fifty-six point eight percent in Novara. Smaller businesses, particularly those with fewer than fifty employees, concentrate a large part of the demand, absorbing fifty-six percent of entries in Biella and Vercelli and as much as sixty-nine percent in Verbano Cusio Ossola. For those evaluating professional opportunities in the area, orienting themselves towards targeted training or consolidating vertical skills represents an obligatory step to overcome selections.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). An analysis of the Excelsior survey data also offers operational insights for those looking at the cross-border labor market or evaluating professional mobility options between border regions and neighboring Swiss cantons. With demand strongly oriented towards services, trade, and catering, and a widespread requirement for personnel with specific prior experience, candidates must structure their job search by focusing on a CV that strongly highlights practical skills gained in the field. Those intending to evaluate employment opportunities in Upper Piedmont or manage a career transition path can use dedicated digital tools to match their skills with the real needs of local companies and neighboring provinces. To explore active offers and understand which sectors are experiencing the greatest personnel shortages, it is advisable to constantly consult the specialized sections.
### Tools and resources for active job searching
Planning a new career phase requires the use of targeted tools to evaluate not only open positions, but also the economic sustainability of employment, taking into account the tax, social security, and salary specificities that characterize the area and neighboring territories. For those moving or evaluating labor mobility between Italy and Switzerland, access to financial simulation platforms and punctual comparison between different job opportunities help in making informed choices. To analyze available job offers and identify companies actively hiring in the region, you can access the section dedicated to [job listings](nav:jobs). If instead you wish to examine company profiles in detail and understand which industrial or service entities offer the greatest guarantees of contractual stability, check the opportunities on the page dedicated to [hiring companies](nav:companies). To better plan your economic and tax position in relation to expected income, you can use the [tax calculator](nav:calculator).

item.title: Living in Cucciago and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Discover the advantages and disadvantages of living at Cucciago and working in Ticino as a border worker. Information on transportation, cost of living and taxes.
item.content:encoded:
## Living in Cucciago and working in Ticino as a cross-border commuter
Cucciago is a Swiss municipality located in the Canton of Ticino, a few kilometers from Lugano. It is a quiet and picturesque residential area, ideal for those who wish to live in a peaceful environment while still being close to the city. Thanks to its strategic location, Cucciago offers its residents the opportunity to work in Ticino and enjoy all the benefits that come with it.
### In brief - **Distance from Lugano**: 15 km - Travel time: 20 minutes by car - Cost of living: Lower than Lugano - Recommended areas: Historic center, residential neighborhood
### Cost of living The cost of living in Cucciago is generally lower than in Lugano. For example, the average price of a 3-room apartment in Cucciago is around CHF 350,000, while in Lugano it can exceed CHF 500,000. Food and service prices are also more contained in Cucciago.
### Transportation Cucciago is well connected to Lugano and other Ticino municipalities via the road and rail network. Cucciago railway station is on the Lugano-Milan line and offers direct connections to the main Swiss and Italian cities.
### Work The Canton of Ticino is an important economic region, with one of the lowest unemployment rates in Switzerland. The main industries are tourism, finance, and technology. Those who work in Ticino can enjoy a higher average salary compared to other Swiss regions.
### Regulations Cross-border commuters working in Ticino must have a Swiss work permit. The permit can be requested online on the Canton of Ticino website. The cost of the permit is CHF 100 per year.
### Operational checklist - Find accommodation in Cucciago - Register with the municipality of residence - Request a Swiss work permit - Open a Swiss bank account - Take out Swiss health insurance
### Comparison of practical scenarios #### Scenario 1: Working in Lugano and living in Cucciago - Advantages: Savings on cost of living, peaceful environment - Disadvantages: Travel time by car, possible difficulties in finding parking in Lugano
#### Scenario 2: Working and living in Cucciago - Advantages: Peaceful environment, lower cost of living - Disadvantages: Possible difficulties in finding work in Cucciago, social isolation
In conclusion, living in Cucciago and working in Ticino as a cross-border commuter can be an excellent solution for those who wish to live in a peaceful environment while still being close to the city. Thanks to its strategic location, Cucciago offers its residents the opportunity to work in Ticino and enjoy all the benefits that come with it. ## Transportation Cucciago is well connected with Lugano and the rest of Ticino thanks to an efficient bus network. The nearest train station is in Lugano, which offers connections to major Swiss and Italian cities. By car, Cucciago can be reached via the A2/A9 motorway. The travel time from Lugano is about 20 minutes, while from Milan it is about an hour and a half. For those who prefer cycling, there are several bike paths that connect Cucciago to Lugano and other locations in Ticino.
## Accommodation In Cucciago, cross-border workers can find various accommodation options, from apartments to houses. Property prices are generally lower compared to Lugano, but it is important to also consider the costs of daily transportation. For example, a 3-room apartment in Cucciago can cost around 1,500 CHF per month, while the same type of apartment in Lugano can cost over 2,500 CHF.
## Work Ticino offers various job opportunities for cross-border workers, especially in the tourism, healthcare, and finance sectors. Lugano is the main economic center of the canton and hosts numerous international companies. The average salary in Ticino is about 5,500 CHF per month, but can vary significantly depending on the sector and job position.
## Regulations Cross-border workers who work in Ticino must have a Swiss work permit. The permit can be requested by the Swiss employer or directly by the worker at the Labor Office of the canton of Ticino. The cost of the permit is 300 CHF per year. Additionally, cross-border workers must also have Swiss health insurance.
## Comparisons For a cross-border worker who works in Ticino, living in Cucciago can be a good solution to save on accommodation and transportation costs. However, it is important to also consider travel times and the availability of public transportation. For example, a cross-border worker who works in Lugano and lives in Cucciago will need to spend about 200 CHF per month on public transportation, while a cross-border worker who lives in Lugano and works in Milan will need to spend about 500 CHF per month on transportation.
## Checklist - Check the availability of accommodation in Cucciago and the related costs - Compare travel times and public transportation costs between Cucciago and Lugano - Get information on Swiss regulations regarding work permits and health insurance - Evaluate job opportunities in Ticino and the related salaries - Consider additional costs, such as expenses for bicycles or cars
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Cost of living and taxes The cost of living in Cucciago is generally lower than in Lugano, but still higher than in other Italian border towns. Property prices are more affordable and the quality of life is high. As for taxes, cross-border workers are subject to withholding tax in Switzerland and must declare their income in Italy as well. It is important to be aware of the tax conventions between Switzerland and Italy to avoid double taxation.
### Cost of living In Cucciago, the cost of living is lower than in Lugano, but still higher than in other Italian border towns. Property prices are more affordable and the quality of life is high.
### Taxes Cross-border workers are subject to withholding tax in Switzerland and must declare their income in Italy as well. It is important to be aware of the tax conventions between Switzerland and Italy to avoid double taxation.
### Tax conventions The tax conventions between Switzerland and Italy are important to avoid double taxation. Switzerland signed a tax convention with Italy in 1992, which came into force in 1993. This tax convention provides that cross-border workers are subject to withholding tax in Switzerland and must declare their income in Italy as well.
### Double taxation Double taxation is a problem that can occur when working in a country different from the one in which you reside. In this case, cross-border workers who work in Ticino and reside in Italy could be subject to paying taxes in both countries. However, the tax convention between Switzerland and Italy provides that cross-border workers are subject to withholding tax in Switzerland and must declare their income in Italy as well. This means that cross-border workers should not be subject to paying taxes in both countries.
### Operational checklist - Check your tax situation with a tax consultant - Declare your income in Italy - Pay withholding tax in Switzerland - Be aware of the tax conventions between Switzerland and Italy

item.title: Vote on Pecc in the Grand Council: the economic choice
item.description: Appeal of economic and environmental organizations to the Grand Council of Ticino for the vote on the Cantonal Energy and Climate Plan.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Appeal to the Grand Council on the Pecc - Economic choice and energy transition - Reduction of fossil fuels - 8 billion in energy imports
## Key facts - **What**: Open letter to the Grand Council for the vote on the Cantonal Energy and Climate Plan - When: Ahead of next week's vote in Canton Ticino - Where: Canton Ticino - Who: Economic, consumer, and environmental organizations including WWF, Aeeticino, Acsi, Federlegno, Swissolar, App, and ProNatura - Amount: 8 billion francs spent every year to import fossil energy into Switzerland
The economic, consumer, and environmental organizations of Canton Ticino have written directly to all 90 members of the Grand Council ahead of the vote on the Cantonal Energy and Climate Plan (Pecc), scheduled for next week in the Grand Council. The joint appeal is signed by WWF, Aeeticino, Acsi, Federlegno, Swissolar, App, and ProNatura, who are asking for the measure to proceed straight ahead and be approved without delay. In the letter sent to the cantonal parliamentarians, it is emphasized that recent climate events represent a warning bell that cannot be ignored. The heatwave and drought recorded during the summer were an obvious signal prompting the associations to demand decisive and timely political action. The debate on the Cantonal Energy and Climate Plan thus moves to the heart of the Ticino political arena, mobilizing not only the environmentalist front but also local economic and consumer representatives.
### Economic and strategic motivations
The central argument put forward by the signatory organizations is not based solely on the need to combat climate change, but emphasizes the strong economic value of the energy transition. According to the associations, accelerating the shift towards renewable sources represents a strategic and advantageous choice that directly benefits households. Reducing fossil fuel consumption does not only mean decreasing polluting emissions, but also implies the ability to invest within Switzerland those billions of francs that currently systematically flow abroad. This change would increase the country's overall energy independence while giving a strong boost to the local economy, employment, and technological innovation. For these reasons, the deputies of the Ticino Grand Council are invited to strongly support the Pecc and the consequent modification of the Energy Law proposed by the Council of State, a regulatory text specifically designed to accelerate the transition towards ecological heating and renewable energy sources. The importation of fossil energies currently represents a colossal expense item for the Confederation, with figures that weigh heavily on the trade balance and national energy security, prompting associations to demand an immediate change of course through the approval of the institutional measures provided for by the cantonal legislative package. The in-depth analysis presented by the organizations that signed the open letter highlights macroeconomic data of considerable importance for understanding the scope of current energy dependence. Switzerland, at present, imports fossil fuels every year for a total estimated expenditure of around 8 billion francs. This massive outflow of capital results in a level of foreign energy dependence that stands at approximately 68%. This structural vulnerability is essentially attributable precisely to fossil fuels, which continue to be 100% imported from external markets. Completing the energy transition means, according to the promoters of the appeal addressed to the Ticino Grand Council members, redirecting the billions of francs that are currently allocated to the import of harmful energy sources towards local resources and productive sectors capable of generating real added value directly in the territory of the Canton of Ticino.
### Impacts on productive sectors and local grids
The positive repercussions of this transformation affect multiple sectors of the Ticinese and Swiss economy. District heating networks need to be carefully planned and constantly maintained, while heat pumps and electric vehicles are powered using electricity produced locally in the valleys and on the roofs of buildings. Photovoltaic systems and energy renovation interventions also represent a stable and continuous source of work for installers, industry professionals, and the entire local construction supply chain. Conversely, oil and its derivatives continue to be exclusively imported at a high price, without leaving lasting added value to the cantonal economy. Added to this picture is the factor linked to the evolution of energy costs on the markets. While we are witnessing yet another wave of price increases regarding fossil fuel prices, average data relating to electricity in Switzerland show a downward trend: average prices fell by 10% in 2025 and 4% in 2026, while a further reduction of 4% is already budgeted and planned for the course of 2027 as well, offering a further element of economic advantage in favor of solutions based on renewable electricity.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). The discussion on the Cantonal Energy and Climate Plan is part of a broader context of climate urgency that does not spare Swiss territory. The arguments submitted to the 90 members of the Grand Council emphasize that in Switzerland climate change is manifesting at twice the speed of the global average. This phenomenon brings growing consequences and damages affecting various strategic areas, including agriculture, public health, biodiversity, and the safety of infrastructure and citizens. Extreme events such as the drought and heatwaves recorded in 2026, as well as the tragic floods and landslides that struck the Maggia Valley and Mesolcina in 2024, constitute dramatic reminders of territorial vulnerability. More and more goods cross the Swiss Alps, but road transport grows more than twice as fast as rail transport. This is reported by the Federal Office of Transport in its semi-annual reports. Rail freight traffic grew by 3.1%, while truck transport increased by 7%. As a result, the rail sector saw its market share decrease by 0.9 percentage points to 68%. Meanwhile, 511,000 trucks have already been transited and the UFT predicts that, by the end of the year and for the first time in a long time, the overall share will once again exceed the threshold of one million heavy vehicles along the crossings. item.title: Frontier workers in Laveno-Mombello: driving and tax in Ticino
item.description: Living in Laveno-Mombello and working in Ticino: connections, taxes at source, deductibles and pension for frontier workers.
item.content:encoded:
## In Brief - Laveno-Mombello in the province of Varese offers connections to Canton Ticino. - The New Agreement regulates taxation and treatments between Italy and Switzerland. - Tax exemption threshold of 10,000 euros for new cross-border workers and 7,500 euros for existing ones.
## Key Facts - **What**: Commuting and residency guide for cross-border workers on Lake Maggiore - When: New Agreement in force since January 1, 2024 - Where: Laveno-Mombello (Varese) and Canton Ticino - Who: Workers with a G permit and Swiss employers - Amount: IRPEF exemption threshold up to 10,000 euros for new cross-border workers
The municipality of Laveno-Mombello, located on the Lombard shore of Lake Maggiore in the province of Varese, represents a residential hub for those working across the border. Those who choose this location to establish their home must carefully consider the distances in kilometers and the logistical variables linking the province of Varese with the main industrial and service hubs of Canton Ticino, such as Bellinzona, Locarno, and Lugano. The commute to the road border crossings or rail connections requires careful planning to manage daily travel times, influenced by both lakeside traffic and the main roads leading toward the border customs.
### Border Crossings and Connections to Ticino To reach Swiss territory from Laveno-Mombello, workers mainly use the road links heading toward the border crossings of upper Varese, including Zenna, Fornasette, and Ponte Tresa, or choose to travel down along standard roads leading to the Brogeda motorway crossing or the Gaggiolo customs depending on their specific workplace. As an alternative to road transport, the railway network offers services connecting local stations with Swiss transport hubs. Every cross-border worker operating in Switzerland with a G permit must assess out-of-pocket commuting costs and verify the most convenient route in advance via the [border crossing map](nav:border-map) to optimize travel time. ## Tax Regime Between Switzerland and Italy
The regulatory framework for individuals residing in Laveno-Mombello and working in the Swiss Confederation is defined by the New Agreement signed on December 23, 2020, which formally entered into force on January 1, 2024, following Italian ratification through Law 83 of June 13, 2023. Bilateral tax relations are grounded in the Double Taxation Convention signed on December 9, 1976, taking into account that Switzerland is neither a member of the European Union nor of the European Economic Area.
### Withholding Tax and IRPEF Allowances Withholding tax on employment income is deducted directly by the Swiss employer according to the tax rates applicable in the canton of employment. The Italian tax system does not apply a duplicate withholding on the payslip: to prevent double taxation, Italy grants a foreign tax credit to be claimed under section CE of the tax return. The regulations distinguish between two categories of taxpayers: - Workers classified as 'old cross-border commuters', who held this status prior to July 17, 2023, benefit from a transitional regime valid from 2024 to 2033 with an exempt threshold of 7,500 euros on Swiss income, alongside the tax reimbursement mechanism (ristorni) paid to border municipalities. - Workers classified as 'new cross-border commuters' are subject to concurrent taxation in Italy but are entitled to an IRPEF tax-free allowance of 10,000 euros.
The remaining taxable income declared to the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) is subject to the standard national IRPEF tax brackets: 23% up to 28,000 euros, 35% between 28,001 and 50,000 euros, and 43% over 50,000 euros. Individual financial outcomes depend on gross income and applicable deductions, which you can estimate using the dedicated [tax calculator](nav:calculator).
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ## Social security, healthcare coverage, and practical management
Alongside tax regulations, cross-border commuters working in Switzerland must fulfill Swiss social security and pension contribution obligations. Mandatory statutory deductions regulated at the federal level apply to monthly earnings. These include the employee's share of the first pillar (AVS/AI/IPG) equal to 5.3%, the unemployment insurance contribution (AD/AC) of 1.1% up to an annual ceiling of CHF 148,200, non-occupational accident insurance (LAINF) with rates ranging from 0.7% to 1.5%, and the second pillar occupational pension (LPP), which entails rates between 7% and 18% depending on the age bracket starting at age 25.
### Health insurance and the right of option Regarding healthcare protection, workers holding a G permit have the right of option between the Swiss statutory health insurance system (LAMal) and enrollment in the Italian National Health Service (SSN) through INPS. By choosing LAMal, cross-border workers take out a private insurance policy with annual adult deductibles ranging between CHF 300 and CHF 2,500, benefiting from targeted medical coverage. This decision is binding and directly affects the household's monthly fixed expenses.
Evaluating whether to move to or remain in Laveno-Mombello therefore requires balancing rental and real estate costs on the eastern shore of Lake Maggiore with commuting expenses, social security contributions, and applicable tax brackets upon returning home. Before signing a contract or completing a change of residence, check the net economic impact on your paycheck using the [salary calculator](nav:calculator).

However, it is crucial to analyze in detail all aspects that characterize this cross-border life choice. The new Cross-Border Commuter Agreement, which came into effect on January 1, 2024, has introduced significant changes in terms of taxation and allowances, modifying the framework for those who choose to reside in Italy and work in Switzerland. The Italian ratification, carried out through Law 83 of June 13, 2023, made the new provisions effective. For the so-called 'old cross-border commuters,' those who already enjoyed this status before July 17, 2023, a tax exemption of CHF 7,500 is provided, with a transitional regime extending until 2033. For 'new cross-border commuters,' however, the allowance has been set at CHF 10,000. These amounts represent a threshold of income that is not subject to tax in Switzerland but is subsequently recovered in Italy through the tax credit mechanism, provided for in section CE of the 730 model. Withholding tax, in fact, is levied exclusively in Switzerland. Italy, through the aforementioned tax credit, thus avoids double taxation. The Double Taxation Agreement between Italy and Switzerland, signed on December 9, 1976, continues to be the regulatory framework for managing fiscal relations between the two states, considering that Switzerland is not a member of the European Union or the European Economic Area. Understanding these tax dynamics is the first step towards effective planning of one's work and income situation. ### Commuting and Cost of Living: Pigra and Ticino

Beyond logistical aspects, the cost of living represents another determining factor. Although Pigra may offer a lower average cost of living compared to the urban centers of the Canton of Ticino, it is essential to compare the prices of consumer goods, services, and housing. The purchasing power generated by Ticino salaries, even taking into account withholding taxes and Swiss contributions, must be related to the expenses incurred in the Italian residence area. For example, Swiss contributions for employees include AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3%, AD/AC at 1.1% (with a cap of CHF 148,200), LAINF with a rate between 0.7% and 1.5%, and LPP (Pension Fund) with variable rates between 7% and 18% depending on the age group (starting from 25 years old). These amounts, added to the Swiss withholding tax, must be compared with Italian taxes, which have progressive rates (23% up to €28,000, 35% between €28,001 and €50,000, 43% over €50,000). Understanding these financial flows is fundamental to evaluating the overall economic convenience of the housing choice in Pigra in relation to working in Ticino. It is equally important to consider insurance, particularly LAMal (health insurance), for which cross-border commuters have the right of option, with deductibles for adults ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500.

Before making the decision to live in Pigra and work in Ticino a reality, it is necessary to address a series of practical steps and considerations. Firstly, it is essential to obtain detailed information about the new cross-border worker agreement, in effect since January 1, 2024. Withholding tax remains an exclusive deduction for Switzerland, while Italy applies a tax credit to avoid double taxation, managed through the CE section of the Modello 730 tax return. Regarding health insurance, cross-border workers have the option to choose between Swiss mandatory insurance (LAMal) and Italian insurance, with different deductibles and coverages to be carefully evaluated. LAMal deductibles for adults can range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. The choice of health insurance has direct implications on costs and medical coverage. It is also advisable to inquire about the procedures for obtaining a work and residence permit, although for residents in Italy working in Ticino, this primarily concerns the G permit. Simulating your net salary, taking into account all these factors, can provide a clear picture of your financial situation. It is also recommended to verify any specific agreements between the employer in Ticino and the Italian tax authorities to ensure compliance with all current regulations. item.title: AVS 2030: the Swiss pension reform
item.description: The AVS 2030 reform was presented in Bern. Extra income estimated at 600 million per year and increase in minimum age from 58 to 63 years. Divisions between parties.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - AHV 2030 reforms Swiss social security - Estimated extra revenue of 600 million annually - Minimum age increases from 58 to 63 years - Right and left divided on measures
## Key facts - What: Reform of the first pillar AHV 2030-2040 - When: Bill presented on May 20, 2024 - Where: Bern - Who: Federal Council and Elisabeth Baume-Schneider - Amount: 600 million Swiss francs per year until 2040
While the government aims for new revenues and a gradual increase in the minimum retirement age, social partners remain dissatisfied with the proposed measures. Although everyone agrees on the need to reform the AHV, the recipes for doing so differ sharply. In Lugano as in Mendrisio, cross-border workers and residents look at these changes with apprehension, fearing repercussions on their purchasing power. While the left welcomes the project, the right and Ticino economic associations complain about the absence of structural reforms, such as an increase in the retirement age, currently set at 65 for everyone.
At the time of the bill presentation on May 20, Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider justified the reform with the need for the first pillar to best prepare for the retirement of the so-called baby boomers, born between 1946 and 1964. In short, the AHV must be revised to adapt it to Switzerland's demographic evolution for the 2030-2040 period. The project is expected to generate additional revenues of about 600 million Swiss francs per year until 2040. For this reason, the executive refrains from increasing, for now, the general reference age.
### The context of the government reform Among the main measures stands out the progressive increase of the minimum age for early retirement, which will go from 58 to 63 years to cope with the increase in life expectancy, which has risen to an average of 83 years in the Confederation, and the shortage of skilled labor in key sectors such as healthcare and the Ticino mechanical industry. The stated objective is to ensure that workers remain active for as long as possible. However, some exceptions are foreseen, particularly in the event of company restructuring or within collective employment agreements with specific clauses, but it would still not be possible to drop below 60 years.
After 65 years, employees, including the approximately 90,000 cross-border workers active in Canton Ticino, should also have the option to remain affiliated with a second-pillar pension institution to fill any contribution gaps. The executive also aims to introduce new reduction rates in the event of early collection of the pension, calculated on an actuarial basis to avoid underfunding of the fund.
Other measures include the alignment of the contribution rate for self-employed workers with high incomes to that of employees, set at 8.7% instead of the current 8.1%, as well as the subject to contribution of excessive dividends distributed by corporations and limited liability companies. Currently, in fact, dividends are not subject to AHV social contributions, which can induce entrepreneurs to favor them over taxable salary, partly evading social security levies. The reactions of the political and economic world to the AHV 2030 reform highlight a deep split between the factions, with financial allocations that directly affect the approximately 80,000 cross-border workers active in Ticino. Unsurprisingly, the Socialist Party and the Greens welcome the Federal Council's decision not to raise the retirement age to 67, a parameter that would have penalized the workforce active in the industrial hubs of Mendrisio and Lugano. The Socialist Party supports measures aimed at closing contribution gaps, including the obligation to pay contributions on daily sickness and accident allowances, thus protecting those working in the tertiary and healthcare sectors. There is also consensus on the income-related reduction percentages in the event of early retirement, allowing low-income workers to retire earlier with smaller losses. Furthermore, the Socialist Party and the Greens demand better recognition of educational and care work, requesting that credits in the first pillar be significantly increased and also applied in occupational pension provision, given that it is primarily women who perform this work, suffering lower pensions.
### Criticisms from the center-right and economy Bourgeois parties instead criticize the project, defining it as insufficient in the face of an estimated deficit of over 4 billion francs by 2030. The FDP.The Liberals hopes for a higher reference age instead of an increase in taxes and contributions, while the Swiss People's Party demands cuts to federal spending to stabilize the AHV. The center notes the lack of structural measures and proposes a model based on the overall duration of working life. Business circles also reject the project. The economic world hopes for structural reforms rather than a simple increase in revenues, fearing repercussions on the competitiveness of companies based in border municipalities such as Chiasso or Stabio. Economiesuisse defines the project as disappointing, since the debate on the reference age is missing. The Swiss Trade Union Federation instead welcomes the coverage of contribution gaps, but criticizes the raising of the minimum age in the second pillar, which would make early retirement more difficult for people with health problems. Several cantons oppose the raising of the minimum age in the second pillar, but positively evaluate the abandonment of a higher reference age. However, Zurich believes that an adjustment is inevitable in the long term to guarantee the sustainability of the system at current rates.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). To get your bearings on the changes envisaged by the AVS reform and to understand the effects on your social security and contribution position, it is necessary to follow the evolution of the institutional debate in Bern. New arrangements for contribution rates, such as adjustment for the self-employed and examination of dividends, require attention from those managing complex incomes. A border worker domiciled in Lugano who receives 90,000francs per year will see an increase in tax levies estimated at 0.3% from 1 January 2026, directly affecting the monthly net.
Monitoring legislative deadlines allows you to anticipate the impacts on your pension plan and accurately assess retirement planning in Switzerland. Those who work in Chiasso or Mendrisio must consider the progressive alignment of the retirement age of women to 65 by 2028, introduced by the federal law of 17 December 2021.
To better manage the transition, it is advisable to follow an operational checklist: check the AVS account statement at the Compensation Fund of the Canton of Ticino in Bellinzona, analyse the payments of the second pillar (LPP) and possibly plan voluntary redemptions before the end of the fiscal year. To explore the contribution aspects and calculate the impact on your income, you can use the [calcolatore fiscale](nav:calculator) available online.

## Key facts - **What**: Living in Fino Mornasco while working in the Canton of Ticino - When: Regulatory framework in effect since January 1, 2024 - Where: Fino Mornasco (Province of Como) and Canton of Ticino - Who: Resident workers with a G permit - Amount: IRPEF tax-free allowance of €10,000 for new cross-border workers
Fino Mornasco is strategically located in the southern outskirts of Como, attracting those who wish to work cross-border while maintaining lower housing costs compared to municipalities immediately adjacent to the border. Anyone planning to live in Fino Mornasco and work in Ticino as a cross-border worker primarily evaluates transport intermodality and distance from main customs checkpoints.
### Transport logistics and travel times
The presence of a motorway exit on the A9 Lainate-Como-Chiasso allows you to reach the Brogeda border crossing in about fifteen to twenty minutes under normal traffic conditions. However, during morning peak hours, queues entering the commercial and tourist customs checkpoint can significantly extend travel times to Lugano or Mendrisio. The road alternative includes secondary routes towards smaller crossings in the Como area, which are useful on days of heavy congestion.
On the rail public transport front, the town's railway station guarantees frequent services to Como San Giovanni and the Brianza region. From Como, you can board TILO regional trains heading to Chiasso, Bellinzona, and the rest of the Canton of Ticino. For those seeking a comfortable journey without the stress of customs queues, the train option represents a solid and economically sustainable choice. You can check road traffic conditions by consulting the [border crossing wait times](nav:border). ...

Healthcare management requires specific attention immediately after starting employment. Cross-border workers have the right to choose between the Italian national health system (by enrolling in INPS/SSN coverage) and the Swiss mandatory LAMal insurance. Adult deductibles in the Swiss system range from 300 to 2,500 francs per year, a factor to weigh against one’s health conditions and family responsibilities. Before formalizing the move to Fino Mornasco, one must also assess the impact of currency exchange on savings, since daily living expenses in Italy are paid in euros against a salary earned in Swiss francs.
### Practical steps for relocation
To organize the move efficiently, it is advisable to follow a structured, sequential process: - Register the new official residence at the Municipality of Fino Mornasco as soon as the rental or purchase contract for the property is available. - Notify the Swiss employer and the competent cantonal migration office of the address update for the adjustment of the G permit. - Consider opening a multi-currency bank account to optimize conversions and monitor market fluctuations. - Formally exercise the right of option regarding health coverage within the deadlines set by cantonal regulations. - Prepare Swiss income documents to fulfill annual declaration obligations with the Italian Revenue Agency.
The combination of a favorable road network towards Brogeda and balanced housing quality makes Fino Mornasco a frequent destination for cross-border workers in the Como area. item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Explosion at the Ritom hydroelectric plant. - Partial collapse of the historic 1917 structure. - Two workers seriously injured. - Investigations underway into the causes.
## Key facts - **What**: Explosion and partial collapse of hydroelectric plant. - When: Wednesday morning, September 9, 2026, around 9:30. - Where: Ritom hydroelectric plant, Piotta, Alta Leventina (Canton Ticino). - Who: Injured workers, firefighters, medical personnel, cantonal police. - Details: Historic structure dating from 1917, powered the Gotthard railway line.
A sudden explosion shook the morning of Wednesday, September 9, 2026, around 9:30, inside the historic Ritom hydroelectric plant. The plant, located in Piotta, in the Alta Leventina, Canton Ticino, was the scene of a serious incident that caused the partial collapse of its original structure, dating back to 1917. This historic plant played a crucial role in supplying electricity to the Gotthard railway line, a key artery for national connections and potentially for the transit of goods and people, including cross-border workers who use this route. The structural collapse had immediate and dramatic consequences, sweeping away two people who were inside the plant at the moment of the explosion. The two workers sustained serious injuries, requiring a prompt and effective response from rescuers. The rescue operation was immediately activated on site, with the intervention of the Biasca and Alta Leventina fire brigades, assisted by the medical personnel of Tre Valli Soccorso. To ensure the urgent transport of the injured to hospital in the shortest possible time, a Rega helicopter was also deployed, underscoring the gravity of the situation and the need for immediate specialist medical care. The cantonal police promptly cordoned off and secured the entire perimeter of the plant, a necessary measure to allow both the delicate rescue operations and the subsequent technical surveys indispensable for understanding the dynamics of the event. The exact causes of the explosion remain unknown at present, a detail that has led the investigating authorities to open a thorough investigation. The aim of the investigation is to clarify the exact dynamics of the incident, identify any pre-existing structural weaknesses or anomalies in the infrastructure that may have contributed to the explosion, in order to prevent similar future incidents. The safety of critical infrastructures, such as those that power strategic railway lines, is a matter of primary importance to ensure service continuity and the safety of workers and citizens. The Gotthard line, in particular, also plays a significant role for the Ticino economy and commuter flows, making every disruption or incident an event to be monitored closely for its potential repercussions. Authorities are working to gather all necessary information to reconstruct what happened and to establish any possible responsibilities. The partial collapse of the historic structure adds an additional layer of complexity to recovery operations and investigations, given the historical and structural importance of the building. The priority remains the health of the injured and the securing of the area. Investigations will continue in the coming days to shed full light on the incident and its deep causes, providing updates as new verifiable details emerge. Managing a facility of this scale requires high safety standards and rigorous periodic checks, an aspect that will certainly be at the heart of the ongoing verifications by the competent authorities. The reconstruction of the plant, if necessary, and the full reactivation of the Gotthard railway line will depend on the outcome of the investigations and subsequent technical assessments. Public attention is now focused on the condition of the injured and the progress of the investigations aimed at establishing the truth about the explosion. Transparency in communications regarding the incident will be fundamental to maintain the trust of citizens and sector operators. Further information will be disseminated as soon as available and verified by the competent authorities, in accordance with the ongoing investigative procedures. The stability and reliability of Swiss energy infrastructures are crucial for the country. The accident at the Ritom hydroelectric power plant, although an event limited to a specific infrastructure, raises questions about the safety of energy networks that support essential services such as rail transport. The Gotthard line, in fact, is not only a vital artery for Switzerland, but also a fundamental connection for commuters who cross the border between Italy and Canton Ticino every day for work. Although the source does not specify a direct impact on border crossers' flows or travel times due to this accident, it is permissible to consider the potential indirect implications arising from an interruption or slowdown on the railway line. A malfunction or damage to such a strategic plant could, in theory, result in temporary changes to rail services, forcing border crossers to look for alternative routes or suffer unforeseen delays. The dependence on the power grid provided by the Ritom plant for the operation of the Gotthard line makes this incident a reminder of the importance of maintaining very high safety standards for all critical infrastructure. Ongoing investigations will need to ascertain whether there was negligence or whether the event was caused by unforeseen factors, but the outcome will certainly have a bearing on future plant maintenance and updating policies.

item.title: Frontier workers in Lugano: question from the Municipality
item.description: Omar Wicht questions the Municipality of Lugano about the hiring of border workers since 2024. A request for clarity on the number, dicasteries and reasons for the selections in the public sector.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Interrogazione del consigliere Wicht (Lega) sulle assunzioni di frontalieri (permesso G) a Lugano dal 2024 al 31 agosto 2026 - Normativa comunale prevede ricorso a manodopera d'oltreconfine solo in "necessità estrema" - Richiesta dati specifici: numero assunti, dicasteri, funzioni, motivi degli scartamenti di candidati svizzeri
## Fatti chiave - **Chi**: Omar Wicht, consigliere comunale della Lega - Cosa: Interrogazione al Municipio di Lugano su assunzioni di frontalieri (permesso G) e cittadini stranieri (permessi B, C, L) - Quando: Periodo coperto: dal 2024 al 31 agosto 2026 - Dove: Lugano, Canton Ticino - Regolamento: Ricorso a manodopera d'oltreconfine "unicamente in caso di necessità estrema e comprovata mancanza di candidati idonei residenti"
---
Il consigliere comunale della Lega Omar Wicht ha presentato un'interrogazione al Municipio di Lugano volta a fare chiarezza sull'assunzione di frontalieri e cittadini stranieri presso l'amministrazione comunale. La richiesta copre il periodo dal 2024 al 31 agosto 2026 e mira a ottenere dati specifici sulla gestione delle risorse umane in ambito transfrontaliero, un tema sensibile nel mercato del lavoro ticinese.
### Quale normativa governa le assunzioni?
Il Regolamento organico dei dipendenti di Lugano e il Regolamento comunale stabiliscono un principio fondamentale: il ricorso a manodopera d'oltreconfine deve essere contemplato unicamente in caso di necessità estrema e comprovata mancanza di candidati idonei residenti. Wicht sottolinea che l'amministrazione comunale è finanziata dai contribuenti luganesi e ticinesi e dovrebbe in primo luogo garantire ricadute economiche, sociali e fiscali sul territorio.
L'interrogazione chiede quanti nuovi frontalieri titolari di permesso G e quanti cittadini stranieri titolari di permessi B, C e L sono stati assunti presso l'amministrazione dal 2024 a oggi, in quale Dicastero, con che funzione e quale grado di occupazione. Wicht vuole inoltre conoscere il motivo per cui la candidatura di cittadini svizzeri non è stata ritenuta idonea nei casi in cui frontalieri o stranieri siano stati assunti.
### Le domande chiave al Municipio
Una delle questioni centrali è se tutte le assunzioni rispondessero effettivamente al criterio di eccezionalità previsto dalla normativa. Wicht chiede per quali profili professionali vi sarebbe stata una comprovata mancanza di personale residente. L'interrogazione affronta anche il tema della concorrenza nel mercato del lavoro: quanti candidati di nazionalità svizzera, e in particolare quanti ticinesi e domiciliati a Lugano, hanno partecipato ai medesimi concorsi e sono stati scartati.
Infine, Wicht pone una questione di principio: il Municipio non ritiene che l'assunzione prioritaria di un cittadino svizzero, meglio ancora se ticinese e residente a Lugano, presso l'amministrazione pubblica porti un beneficio maggiore a tutto il sistema cittadino, cantonale e federale? Questo interrogativo riflette una preoccupazione diffusa nel dibattito politico ticinese sulla priorità da dare al lavoro locale rispetto all'impiego di frontalieri. ### The meaning of "extreme necessity"
The criterion of “extreme necessity” represents a barrier of regulatory protection towards Swiss and resident applicants. It means that a border crossing with a G permit can only access a position at the Lugano municipal administration if no resident candidate is available or eligible for that specific position. In practice, the law pushes the municipalities of Ticino to prioritize the hiring of those who reside in the territory, before resorting to border workers and foreigners.
However, in some technical or specialized professions, the search for suitable resident staff may actually be unsuccessful, justifying the use of border workers. Wicht's question aims to verify whether this principle is applied consistently or whether there are deviations between the regulation and daily administrative practice.
### What situation does the question seek clarity
The question does not yet provide concrete numbers — it asks the Municipality to provide them. item.title: Living in Casnate, working in Ticino
item.description: Moving to Casnate and working in Ticino: tax at source, AVS/LPP and procedures for border workers from 2024.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - New Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - Tax at source withheld ONLY in Switzerland, never in Italy - Excess €7,500 (old cross-border commuters) or €10,000 (new from 2024) - Mandatory LAMal for G border workers in Ticino
## Key facts - **What**: New Italy-Switzerland Border Tax Agreement - When: 1 January 2024 (signed 23 December 2020, ratified Italy Law 83/2023) - Where: Italy-Ticino border - Who: Bilateral agreement between Italy and Switzerland - Deductible: €7,500 (frontier workers before 17/7/2023) or €10,000 (new) - Tax: Withheld exclusively in Switzerland - Contributions: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% employee, AD/AC 1.1%, LPP 7–18% by age group
As of 1 January 2024, those who decide to move to Casnate with Bernate and work in Ticino are facing a new tax framework defined by the New Frontier Agreement. This agreement, signed on 23 December 2020, introduced important innovations on the treatment of tax at source and on deductibles for income from work. The key rule is this: tax at source is only withheld in Switzerland. Italy does not apply withholding taxes and avoids double taxation by granting tax credit in the EC framework of tax return 730.
Border workers who already worked before 17 July 2023 benefit from an exemption of €7,500 per year on gross income; those who start after this date are entitled to a deductible of €10,000. ### How the taxation mechanism works in Switzerland and Italy
The practical procedure is simple: the Ticino employer applies withholding tax to the gross salary net of the allowance. If you work for a company in Lugano with a monthly salary of CHF 4,000, your employer will use the Federal Tax Administration (AFC/ESTV) tables to calculate the amount due. At the end of the working year, you will receive a tax certificate (Steuerbescheinigung) which you will document in your [tax return](nav:tax-return). In Section CE of the Italian 730 form, enter the Swiss tax paid and request the Italian tax credit on the same taxable base.
The Double Taxation Convention between Italy and Switzerland, signed on December 9, 1976, establishes that income from employment is taxed in the country where the service is rendered. Since you work in Ticino, Switzerland has the right to tax. Italy, in turn, does not require a second levy; the credit in the 730 form cancels out the theoretical double taxation.
### G Permit, AVS, LPP and LAMal: the complete package
To work as a cross-border worker in Ticino, you need a [G permit](nav:permits) (maximum limit of 120 days of stay per year in Switzerland). The application is made at the cantonal migration office (SEM/Migration Section of the Canton of Ticino). With a G permit, you automatically become subject to mandatory Swiss contributions: AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3% of the wage bill, occupational pension (LPP) between 7% and 18% depending on age, LAINF accident insurance, and contributions to other funds. These amounts are paid by the employer and you in equal shares or as provided for in the contract.
[LAMal health insurance](nav:health) is mandatory: as a G cross-border worker, you have the option to choose a Swiss health insurance fund or maintain Italian coverage with the right of option. If you choose Swiss LAMal, you will have to pay monthly premiums with an adult deductible ranging between CHF 300 and CHF 2,500 depending on the chosen policy. Many cross-border workers opt for a Ticino LAMal to avoid complications with cross-border declarations.
### Tax refunds: when it is worth applying
At the end of the year, if you have paid withholding tax in Switzerland higher than the actual taxation due (calculated on total income, family, deductions), you are entitled to a [refund](nav:ristorni). The AFC/ESTV processes the declarations and issues refunds by the spring of the following year. For many cross-border workers with a non-working spouse in Italy or dependent children, the refund is significant. The procedure requires submitting the Swiss declaration (A1 form/Simplified declaration) and the Italian declaration (730 or Unico). The two systems synchronize thanks to the information exchanged between administrations.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Practical procedure: steps for moving and starting work
Step 1 — G Permit application. Before starting work, contact the SEM (Migration Office) of Canton Ticino with your employment contract and identity documents. The [G permit](nav:permits) is normally issued within 2–4 weeks. Cost: none.
Step 2 — AVS registration in Switzerland. Your employer will automatically register you in the AVS system (Compensation Fund of Canton Ticino). You will receive your 13-digit AVS number by mail. Keep it: you will need it throughout your career.
Step 3 — Opening a Swiss bank account. It is advisable to open a [CH IBAN account at a Ticino bank](nav:banks) (e.g., UBS, Raiffeisen, Banca Stato Ticino). Your employer will pay your salary into this account. Many banks offer specific accounts for cross-border commuters with favorable EUR/CHF exchange services.
**Step 4 — LAMal subscription.** Within 3 months of starting work, choose a Swiss health insurance fund and sign the policy. If you opt for an Italian fund with the right of option, you must still register with the cantonal administration.
Step 5 — Italian tax return (730 or Unico). By May of the following year, submit the [730 tax return](nav:tax-return) in Italy, including the Swiss tax certificate and the tax credit in section CE. If the Italian employer had suspended the withholding tax, communicate the change in situation to the Revenue Agency (formerly local office).
### Critical deadlines 2024–2025
- June 30, 2024: Deadline for documenting 2023 income for potential adjustments. - May 31, 2025: Submission of the 730 tax return for 2024 income (if resident in Italy). - Calendar year: Request Swiss tax refund within the terms set by the AFC/ESTV (usually until the end of April of the following year). - G Permit renewal: Every 5 years, if the employment relationship continues. Contact SEM with the new contract.
### Tools and resources for calculating net salary
To estimate your net salary, it is useful to use [a specialized calculator for cross-border commuters](nav:calculator), which simulates Swiss withholding tax, allowance, AVS/LPP contributions, and LAMal deductions. This gives you a realistic view of how much you will take home each month. Remember: the gross CHF salary stated in the contract is not the net one. After withholding tax, AVS, LPP, LAINF, and LAMal, the figure drops by about 25–35% depending on the canton, the amount, and the family.
Another valuable tool is the refund comparator, which estimates if you will be entitled to a refund at the end of the year by calculating your total income (including any work in Italy), family deductions, and applicable allowance. If you are married and your spouse does not work, or you have children, the refund increases significantly.

item.title: AVS, the delay on reforms: Economiesuisse's alarm
item.description: Mäder, outgoing President Economiesuisse, criticizes the government: discussion on the postponed retirement age, risks to the sustainability of the system.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Mäder criticizes government: too late on crucial AVS reforms - Retirement age: political taboo, government avoids discussion - Demographic: increasingly serious imbalance between taxpayers and pensioners
## Key facts - **What**: Outgoing President Economiesuisse criticises lack of reforms - When: Recent interview at Tages-Anzeiger - Where: Switzerland, national context - Who: Christoph Mäder (67 years old), former Sandoz and Novartis - Topic: AVS and Swiss social security sustainability
Christoph Mäder raises his voice at the end of his six-year term as President of Economiesuisse. In an interview with Tages-Anzeiger, the 67-year-old is blunt: Switzerland is losing competitiveness to international rivals, and the onus is on the Federal Council's lack of political will to tackle indispensable structural reforms. Mäder, a lawyer and former executive at Sandoz and Novartis, will soon be replaced by Silvan Wildhaber.
The main target of his criticism is the AVS, the Swiss pension system that represents the first pillar of national security. Mäder is very harsh in judging the government's decision to exclude from the next AVS reform any discussion of raising the retirement age:
> “I consider it irresponsible, to use a cautious adjective, to decide not to even discuss retirement age in the upcoming AVS reform.”
### The demographic problem that the government translated text
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Practical Steps: What Cross-Border Workers Should Do
The alarm raised by Mäder, however critical, should not paralyze the cross-border worker: on the contrary, it is all the more reason to prepare actively. Early retirement planning, a prudent scenario that considers possible reforms of the AVS system, diversification between the first and third pillar—all of this reduces the risk of unpleasant surprises at the time of retirement. Those who start planning today have time to adapt to possible changes tomorrow.
### First Step: Verify Your AVS Contribution Status
The first step is to know your contribution history. Every cross-border worker G can request a free copy of the AVS account statement from the compensation fund responsible for the Ticino canton or through the Swiss social security online portal. The statement shows years of contributions accumulated, amounts paid (both employee and employer portions), any contribution gaps, and an estimate of the monthly AVS pension at age 65 (current standard).
This verification is essential to understand your position: how many years remain until retirement, whether there is room to improve your pension, which gaps to fill to maximize future benefits. A careful analysis of your personal file enables realistic planning.
### Specialized Advice for Cross-Border Workers
Given the complexity of the system—which combines Swiss regulations, the 1976 Italian-Swiss tax treaty, the new cross-border agreement in force since January 1, 2024, and possible rights accrued in the Italian system—it is advisable to seek advice from a qualified advisor in cross-border matters. A specialized professional can analyze your personal file (years of Swiss contributions, any Italian contributions, gaps), simulate scenarios with the current retirement age vs. increased age (if the reform is approved), and suggest optimization strategies for the third pillar (pillar 3a) to compensate for any future reductions in AVS.
### Monitor Regulatory Developments
Mäder observes that the government is postponing the discussion on retirement age, but this does not mean that the reform is permanently blocked. It is advisable to stay informed about federal messages, public consultations on AVS reforms, statements from federations like Economiesuisse, and changes in contribution rates (the current 5.3% could increase over time). Constant vigilance on the regulatory front is a tool of protection.
### Evaluate Early or Delayed Retirement
Switzerland allows you to claim AVS starting from an age below 65 (with reductions in the pension) or to defer beyond 65 (receiving increases in the monthly benefit). In the context of uncertainty described by Mäder, the cross-border worker could evaluate both scenarios:
- **Early Retirement**: if you have accumulated a good contribution history, you could decide to retire earlier, accepting a permanent reduction in your pension. This offers greater flexibility in choosing the timing.
- Delayed Retirement: if you want to maximize your pension and have the health to continue, you can work beyond age 65, receiving increases in your monthly benefit. Each additional year of work increases both the contributions paid and the duration of pension payments.
Both scenarios have pros and cons that depend on your personal situation, life expectancy, expected medical costs, and desire for retirement.
### Use the Frontaliere Ticino Online Calculator
The Frontaliere Ticino website offers a [specialized pension calculator](nav:calculator) for cross-border workers that allows you to simulate expected AVS pension at age 65, the effect of a possible increase in retirement age, calculation of early/delayed pension, and integration with the professional pillar if known. This tool, updated with the latest regulations, is one of the fastest ways to get a realistic estimate of your Swiss pension and to compare different scenarios.
